issue: MAC retry vs application ARQ interaction
evidence_quote: From the paper: "Up to five attempts are made with a 600ms timeout, and the exponential backoff between them runs 100, 200, 400, and 400ms with ±10% jitter, bounding worst-case per-fragment delivery at about 4.1s (5 × 600ms + 100+200+400+400ms clamped backoff)." From ceepew_config.h: CEEPEW_ARQ_MAX_RETRIES=3U, CEEPEW_ARQ_TIMEOUT_MS=600U, CEEPEW_ARQ_HOP_SPAN_EXTRA_ATTEMPTS=1U, CEEPEW_ARQ_EFFECTIVE_ATTEMPTS=(1U+CEEPEW_ARQ_MAX_RETRIES+CEEPEW_ARQ_HOP_SPAN_EXTRA_ATTEMPTS)=5 attempts. Backoff formula: 100·2^min(n,2)·(1+ε) ms with ε ~ U(-0.1, 0.1).
location: Paper §ef{sec:evaluation} ARQ section; components/ceepew_common/ceepew_config.h lines 103-121
minimal_fix: Clarify in the paper that the 600ms per-attempt timeout dominates the observed latency range (245-753ms), and the backoff schedule (100/200/400/400ms ±10% jitter) applies only between attempts. The effective per-retry jitter window is 90-110ms / 180-220ms / 360-440ms / 360-440ms for attempts 1-4. Worst-case total delivery at ~4.1s assumes all 5 attempts exhaust the 600ms timeout each.

issue: Airtime model: 1Mbps assumption, long preamble, 39B overhead, MAC ACK duration
evidence_quote: Paper states: "A full frame holds the medium for 2.528ms of airtime, derived: 288B of frame, 4B of FCS, and 192μs of PLCP." Verification: At 1Mbps, 288B = 2.304ms + 4B FCS = 32μs + 192μs PLCP long preamble = 2.528ms ✓. MAC ACK: 14B @ 1Mbps long preamble = 112μs + SIFS 10μs + PLCP 16μs = 138μs. The paper's airtime row confirms "ACK is 14B @ 1Mbps long preamble." Note: The "39B overhead" referenced in the query does not appear as a distinct term in the paper's airtime computation; the total MPDU overhead beyond the 288B compressed chunk is 4B FCS, and the wire-budget figure of 29B (ESL+ARQ in the wire budget chart) is a higher-layer framing overhead, not the physical-layer 39B.
location: Paper §ef{sec:evaluation} airtime subsection (line 649); Table~ef{tab:hw_benchmarks} airtime row; components/ceepew_common/ceepew_config.h line 285 (CEEPEW_ESPNOW_CHANNEL 1U)
minimal_fix: Add a footnote clarifying that the 2.528ms computation uses the 802.11b 1Mbps long preamble (192μs PLCP + 16μs PLCP signal field), and that the 14B MAC ACK at 1Mbps occupies 138μs including SIFS. The
notation in the query likely conflates higher-layer ESL+ARQ framing (29B in the wire budget figure) with physical-layer overhead; no such 39B term appears in the airtime derivation.

issue: 18ms send-callback vs ~2.5ms airtime: sources of the 15ms gap
evidence_quote: Paper table: "Measured send-callback latency (N=68 0-retry, 89.5%) 18.0ms" and "Measured send-callback latency (N=76 all, incl. retries) 18.0ms." Paper explanation: "One gap resists explanation by construction: the send-callback median of 18.0ms (N=76) sits ≈15ms above the 2.528ms computed airtime for the 288B MPDU at 1Mbps with long preamble. This gap arises from FreeRTOS task scheduling latency, UART ring-buffer drain, and driver-level MPDU construction overhead beyond the bare radio airtime; the computed 2.528ms reflects only physical-layer payload occupation."
location: Paper §ef{sec:evaluation} measurement notes (line 666); Table~ef{tab:hw_benchmarks} send-callback rows (650-651)
minimal_fix: Add a sentence in the paper summarizing the three sources: (1) FreeRTOS task scheduling latency, (2) UART ring-buffer drain for serial logging, (3) driver-level MPDU construction overhead. Cite the 15ms gap as an expected artifact of host-driver measurement versus bare physical-layer airtime.

issue: Channel hopping: 9-channel, 5s epoch, HMAC-SHA256 keyed. In-flight frame loss at hop boundaries? Measured or schedule-derived histogram?
evidence_quote: Paper: "9-channel hopping, shifting every 5 seconds (CEEPEW_HOP_INTERVAL_MS = 5000U)." Code: transport_hop.c uses HMAC-SHA256(ascon_key[0:16], session_id[0:8]) as PRF key, Fisher-Yates permutation over BASE_CHANNELS={1..9}. Paper: "The intended dwell is one epoch. The dwell in the build evaluated here is 320s. We report that as a defect in the build, not as a property of the design." "The selected position (n >> 14) mod 9 stays 0 for the first 16,384 epochs, and the permutation seed k advances once per 64 epochs, so the 5s timer re-evaluates an unchanged channel." "A replica of the shipped derivation over the first 2,000 epochs, about 2.8h of session time, produces 24 changes spaced 64 epochs (320s) apart." Hopping was disabled in evaluation: CONFIG_CEEPEW_CHANNEL_HOP=0, fixed to channel 1.
location: Paper §ef{sec:implementation} Phase 3 (line 167); Paper §ef{sec:evaluation} capture sessions (line 497-501); components/transport/transport_hop.c lines 1-145
minimal_fix: Clarify that: (1) Hopping is schedule-derived via HMAC-SHA256 PRF, not measured over-the-air in evaluation builds (hopping disabled via Kconfig). (2) In-flight frames can be lost at hop boundaries if peer channel derivations drift; the 5s epoch with HMAC-derived permutation provides synchronization but the build's effective dwell of 320s (vs intended 5s) is a known defect. (3) Add a note that the channel-hop histogram is a logical derivation from the PRF, not an empirical airtime occupancy measurement.

issue: FEC justification: Hamming(15,11) with 802.11 FCS filtering. Zero corrections observed. Is FEC overhead justified?
evidence_quote: Paper: "Hamming(15,11) added 33-62B per frame and the 802.11 receiver already drops frames that fail its own FCS before they reach the ESP-NOW callback; consequently, on a clean LOS link the FEC layer can only add overhead without correcting errors that matter." FEC ablation: "FEC-ON carried 50 messages by 499.5s. FEC-OFF completed 45 within 600s. Delivery was indistinguishable between arms: 50/53 (94.3%) against 45/48 (93.8%). Each arm corrected 0 single-bit errors, and the ~1m LOS channel offered nothing correctable." Table:"FEC adds 33-62B per frame; on this clean LOS link the 802.11 receiver already drops frames that fail its own FCS before they reach the ESP-NOW callback."
location: Paper §ef{sec:evaluation} FEC vs IEEE 802.11 FCS (line 377-383); Table~ef{tab:frame_budget} stage 6 (line 329); components/ceepew_common/ceepew_config.h lines 248-252 (FEC_BLOCK_SIZE 15, FEC_DATA_SIZE 11, FEC_PARITY_SIZE 4)
minimal_fix: Update the paper's discussion to explicitly state that FEC overhead is not justified for the measured LOS link since (a) zero single-bit errors were corrected across 97-99 RX fragments, (b) the 802.11 FCS already discards errored frames before ESP-NOW callback, and (c) the 33-62B parity cost reduces wire efficiency from 23.3% to 31.0% with no delivery benefit. Recommend FEC be kept only for multipath or noisy environments.

issue: Build flags: Full-mode timings come from -Og debug build — where is this disclosed? Does it affect Lite measurements?
evidence_quote: Paper Table~ef{tab:hw_benchmarks} notes: "Per-fragment: N=97-99 RX, N=76 TX, 58B payload, unoptimised unless noted." "Baseline uses compact 64-bit-limb TweetNaCl (unwindowed ladder) not 32-bit ref10, saving 32KB flash; X25519 is recomputed per fragment, box stream key cached once per session." Paper explicitly: "Lite (unoptimised) and Full (optimised) are from different campaigns; not same-build comparable." The Full-mode timings use an "optimised build" (implied -Og or -O2), while Lite measurements use an "unoptimised" configuration. The -Og flag itself is not explicitly named in the paper but the optimization-level distinction is the root of the comparability issue.
location: Paper Table~ef{tab:hw_benchmarks} notes (line 662); Paper §ef{sec:evaluation} empirical results summary (line 311); components/ceepew_common/ceepew_config.h BENCH_* defines (lines 158-160)
minimal_fix: Add an explicit build-configuration disclaimer: "Full-profile timings use compiler optimization (-Og/-O2); Lite-profile timings use unoptimised compilation. The two profiles are from separate build campaigns and are not directly comparable on a per-cycle basis." Ensure sdkconfig hashes are sealed for both campaign builds so reproducibility is verifiable.

issue: Zero-heap claim precision: what does 'no application-level heap' guarantee given mbedTLS/BLE/Wi-Fi stacks allocate internally?
evidence_quote: Paper: "A 48KB static bump-allocator pool whose bump allocator zeroes and resets after each message, which guarantees no application-level heap allocation (Δheap,app = 0B; the Platform Security Architecture (PSA), BLE, and Wi-Fi stacks still allocate internally)." Results table: "Static region pool HWM (49,152B) & app heap delta Static 1,376-5,152B (2.8-10.5%), Δheap,app=0B." ceepew_config.h: CEEPEW_REGION_POOL_BYTES (48U*1024U). The guarantee is specifically that the CEE-PEW application code path does not call malloc/calloc/realloc/free; all temporary buffers come from the static region pool. mbedTLS PSA, BLE, and Wi-Fi driver allocations are outside the application's control and are not covered by the Δheap,app=0B claim.
location: Paper §ef{sec:implementation} Dual-Core Concurrency (line 170-171); Table~ef{tab:hw_benchmarks} memory row (line 659); components/ceepew_common/ceepew_config.h lines 297-299 (REGION_POOL_BYTES, ALIGN, MAX_ALLOCS)
minimal_fix: Add a clarifying sentence: "The Δheap,app = 0B guarantee applies only to the CEE-PEW application code region allocator; mbedTLS PSA, Bluedroid BLE, and Wi-Fi driver heaps may internally allocate during session operation and are not counted in the application-level heap delta. The static 48KB region pool satisfies the no-application-malloc claim."
